audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 read Skill and 2+ items read K'Sante, against the already-audited mirror (malphite__ksante), which set those two rows to Malphite and Skill.
audit.why: 49.34% over 1218 games. Level 6 is not a wash once Ground Slam's grounding is accounted for — it switches off the All Out dash the whole level-6 plan depends on — and whys[6] itself says 'both reclaim parity', which is Skill, not K'Sante.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side + win[4] -> Malphite (rating 6/10 -> 4/10), phases[6].side + win[6] -> Skill, as matched pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that the page never names a single Malphite ability, and no cooldown appeared anywhere — 'bait his R' with no idea how long it is gone.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100s, Seismic Shard a flat 8s, Ground Slam a flat 7s, Thunderclap 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s. The 7s Ground Slam is the one that actually governs when you may engage.
audit.corrected: All five ability names written in, with 130/115/100s on the ult, 8s on Seismic Shard and 7s on Ground Slam placed where they change a decision.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors, one of them the whole strategy. (1) THE DECISIVE INTERACTION WAS ABSENT: Seismic Shard (Q) and Ground Slam (E) both GROUND, and every piece of K'Sante mobility — Path Maker (W), Footwork (E) and the All Out (R) dash — is a dash. Malphite can switch your entire engage off on a 7s cooldown and the page never mentions it once. (2) 'W's unstoppable' in three paths — Riot's Path Maker text says reduced damage taken, never unstoppable, and the mirror already killed the same error from the other side. (3) 'Q3 knock-up' / 'your third Q knock-up' in four paths — Ntofo Strikes has no knockup or third cast; at 2 stacks it fires a shockwave that pulls.
audit.why: Kit text is the authority. A reader told W makes them unstoppable will charge straight into a Ground Slam that stops the dash outright.
audit.corrected: Grounding written into the interactions row, whys[4], mid, late, spikes[1] and wants.foe[1]; W re-described as a damage-reduced charge; the pull named correctly. Granite Shield's 10%-max-HP absorb added to the itemization row as the thing to break before committing.
sources: kit: Malphite P 'absorbs damage up to 10% of his maximum Health'

audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings claim K'Sante's passive deals MAGIC damage that beats Malphite's armour stacking — the entire stated reason you win long trades.
audit.why: Riot's passive text says only that his abilities mark targets to take more damage on his next attack. No damage type is given, so magic is an assumption, not a fact. The verified armour-beater in his kit is Path Maker's TRUE damage.
audit.corrected: Every 'passive magic damage' claim replaced with Path Maker's true damage, which is flagged in the kit and does the same strategic job honestly.

edits.before: Two tanks farming — this is dead-even until level 3. His Q chips you and slows you toward his W auto, so don't walk straight at him with your tiny early mana pool; last-hit at the tip of your Q instead. The key fact: he stacks armor, and your passive deals magic damage on a marked target, so the longer trades go the more you win them. Just don't get caught by his Q slow with your W charge down.
edits.after: Two tanks farming — this is dead-even until level 3. Seismic Shard chips you and steals your move speed toward his Thunderclap auto, so don't walk straight at him with your tiny early mana pool; last-hit at the tip of your Q instead. The key fact: he stacks armour, and Path Maker deals true damage, so the longer trades go the more you win them. Just don't get caught by his Q with your W charge down.

edits.before: Levels 3 through 5 are your window. Bait his W or Q, then W-charge into him for the terrain stun, Q3 the knock-up, and let your passive magic damage carve his armor-stacked bar — he has no answer to magic in his kit. At 6, All Out is a real 1v1 button here because it survives his R and converts you to a duelist, but it sheds your tankiness, so only pop it to commit a kill or to peel, never to clear a wave. Respect that his R is the one thing that flips a trade — keep W up as your unstoppable answer to his engage.
edits.after: Levels 3 through 5 are your window. Bait his W or Q, then W-charge into him for the terrain stun, land the two-stack Ntofo pull, and let Path Maker's true damage carve his armour-stacked bar — resistances do not answer it. At 6, All Out is a real 1v1 button because it converts you to a duelist, but it sheds your tankiness, so only pop it to commit a kill or to peel, never to clear a wave. The real trap is Ground Slam: on 7s it grounds your W, E and R alike, so never start into a fresh one.

edits.before: It flattens back to even — two control tanks who can't solo-kill each other and both bring an unstoppable engage to teamfights. Your edge is that your passive and Iceborn shred his armor stack while his armor does nothing to your magic; his edge is a longer-range, lower-skill R engage on your carries. Win the side-lane skirmishes with your duelist All Out and use your R to peel his R off your backline. Don't bet on a 1v1 to end it — this lane closes on map pressure, not a kill.
edits.after: It flattens back to even — two control tanks who can't solo-kill each other and both bring a hard engage to teamfights. Your edge is that Path Maker's true damage ignores his armour stack entirely; his edge is a longer-range, lower-skill R engage on your carries, plus two grounding spells that switch your dashes off. Win the side-lane skirmishes with your duelist All Out and use your R to peel his R off your backline. Don't bet on a 1v1 — this lane closes on map pressure, not a kill.

notes: The single biggest gap on this page was that Malphite grounds twice (Seismic Shard, Ground Slam) and K'Sante's W, E and R are all dashes — the mirror flagged the same thing from the other side and it now appears in six paths here. I did NOT assert that Unstoppable Force is genuinely unstoppable-tagged (Riot's text only describes a high-speed launch and knockup), so spikes[3] now leads with its cooldown instead of the word. Whether Path Maker's stun can be tenacity-reduced, and whether Granite Shield recharges mid-combat here, are not in the kit data and were not asserted.
